key_insight: Small random initialization can create a pronounced nonmonotone "accuracy well," where accuracy improves early, drops sharply, and later recovers even as loss changes remain tiny.
engineering_relevance: This warns that training loss alone may miss important classification dynamics, so monitoring accuracy over time is crucial when diagnosing convergence and early stopping.
method: Observed the phenomenon across deep linear, ReLU, and convolutional networks.
Analyzed training under different losses and optimizers on synthetic and benchmark classification tasks.
Developed a rigorous theory for shallow and deep linear networks, including extreme collapse-and-recovery behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical results on MNIST, CIFAR-10, deep linear networks, and controlled synthetic tasks, plus theoretical proofs for linear models and a synthetic case reaching 100% accuracy, then 0, then 100% again.
watch_item: The effect is tied to vanishing/small initialization and may be highly sensitive to training regime, so generalizing conclusions to standard initialization settings should be done cautiously.
paper_title: The Accuracy Well: Nonmonotone Accuracy Dynamics at Vanishing Initialization
